Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Richard Schirrmann, the German schoolteacher who founded the youth hostel movement in Altena, Germany, in 1909. Schirrmann is a surname; the youth-hostel federation he founded does not hold an active marque trademark on his name. 'Stay' frames the brand as a modern lodging.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern hostels have matured into a serious category alongside hotels — design-led, mixed-dorm-and-private, with a kitchen and a common room. The opening is for a brand that names the movement's founder and operates in his register.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Generator Hostels (staygenerator.com) plays the modern reference. Selina (selina.com) holds the lifestyle middle. Freehand (freehandhotels.com) sits in the modern-hotel-hostel crossover. We sit alongside Generator with a heritage-anchor focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: Schirrmann Stay is a modern hostel brand operating in the 1909 youth-hostel register — mixed dorms, shared kitchen, a common room with a stove.

targetAudience.primary: Travellers 22-40 who want a clean dorm bed and a real kitchen, not a hotel room.
behaviors: Book on phone, on the day
Stay three to five nights per city

dos: Name the kitchen and the common room
Publish the dorm bed and the private room rates

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: SCHIRRMANN STAY set in a confident modern grotesk, two words on one line. Small mark: a single stove silhouette used on the door and the breakfast card.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for room rates and the kitchen rota
typography.rationale: A modern grotesk plus its mono — the dorm-ledger register.

Modern.brandDescription: Schirrmann Stay is a modern hostel brand operating in the 1909 youth-hostel register — mixed dorms, shared kitchen, a common room with a stove.
Modern.scope: Schirrmann Stay works across the hostels & budget travel category with a single editorial register.
Modern.mission: Schirrmann Stay is a modern hostel brand operating in the 1909 youth-hostel register — mixed dorms, shared kitchen, a common room with a stove.
Modern.vision: Schirrmann Stay held in its register, indefinitely.

Luxury.tagline: A members' room above the kitchen.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the common kitchen and common room — the shared spaces that have defined the hostel since Altena in 1909. 'Commons Club' reframes the shared-space tradition in a members' register, taking the hostel's social architecture into a poshtel-luxury brand without leaning on a competitor's name.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury hostels (poshtels) are a small editorial category — small properties charging hotel rates for design-led shared-space lodging. The opening is for a brand that takes the common-room architecture seriously.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: The Hoxton (thehoxton.com) plays the design-hotel reference. Soho House (sohohouse.com) holds the members-club middle. Generator (staygenerator.com) sits in the modern-hostel peer. We sit as a luxury hostel in the commons-club register.
Luxury.positioningStatement: The Commons Club is a luxury hostel-and-club where guests pay nightly for a bunk or a private room and members pay annually for the common room.

targetAudience.primary: City travellers 28-50 who want a design-led shared-space lodging and a member's room.
behaviors: Book the same property twice a year
Use the common room as a working day

dos: Name the common room by name
Print all signage in two languages

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: THE COMMONS CLUB set in a classical book serif, three lines centered. Small mark: an embossed key-and-stove crest, used on door cards and the member's pin.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and signage
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and the member's letter
typography.rationale: A classical serif plus a reading serif — the members' club register.

Minimal.tagline: A bed, a locker, a key.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the dormitory bunk — the single object that defines hostel lodging. One word, terminal period. The period is the whole brand statement: nothing more is offered, nothing less.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal hostels serve the traveller who wants a clean bunk and a working lock, nothing more. The category is mostly empty above the budget tier.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most hostels publish a long list of amenities. The minimal end is largely empty. Generator (staygenerator.com) is the closest editorial reference. We sit as the single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Bunk. is a minimal hostel selling one product — a bunk, a locker, and a key — at one fixed nightly rate.

targetAudience.primary: Travellers 22-40 who want a clean bunk and no upsell.
behaviors: Book one night at a time
Carry the key on the lanyard

dos: Name the lock and the locker

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: BUNK. set very large in a clean modern sans, four characters including the period. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for the nightly rate
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-rate register.

Corporate.tagline: Operating the shared spaces, at scale.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the common kitchen — the shared-cooking space that has defined hostels since Altena in 1909. 'Co.' frames the brand as a B2B operator that runs shared-space hospitality assets for owners and franchisees.
Corporate.industrySummary: Hostel operators are a small institutional category — third-party management firms running properties for owners. The opening is for a heritage-anchored operator with a documented common-room playbook.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: A&O Hostels (aohostels.com) plays the institutional peer. Meininger (meininger-hotels.com) holds the multi-property middle. St Christopher's Inns (st-christophers.co.uk) is the heritage chain reference. We sit as a B2B operator with a shared-space playbook.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Common Kitchen Co. is a hostel operations company running shared-space lodging for owners across multi-property portfolios.

targetAudience.primary: Hostel property owners, hospitality investors, and franchise partners.
behaviors: Care about occupancy, length-of-stay, and review scores
Renew on five- to seven-year terms

dos: Lead with the operations playbook and the portfolio
Speak the language of owners and investors
Refer to client properties by name
donts: No social media at the parent level

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: COMMON KITCHEN CO. set in an institutional serif, three lines. A small mark — a stylised kitchen-stove silhouette — used on contracts.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and operating agreements
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the operator register.

Creative.tagline: Pasta, with people you haven't met.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the hostel ritual of cooking pasta in the common kitchen and eating with strangers at the long table. The phrase 'stove & strangers' names the ritual without leaning on a competitor's brand.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative hostels play on a single ritual or social moment as the editorial frame. The common-kitchen pasta dinner is rich and under-used as a brand frame.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Generator (staygenerator.com) plays the editorial reference. Selina (selina.com) holds the lifestyle middle. Freehand (freehandhotels.com) is the design-hostel reference. We sit as a ritual-led creative brand in the common-kitchen register.
Creative.positioningStatement: Stove & Strangers is a creative hostel brand built on the common-kitchen pasta ritual — a long table, a stove, and an open seat at dinner.

targetAudience.primary: Solo travellers 22-40 who want to meet people without trying.
behaviors: Book the dorm with the long table
Cook one night's pasta as a turn
Stay for the dinner, not the room

dos: Print the dinner rota on the kitchen wall
Name the pasta of the night

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: STOVE & STRANGERS set in a warm display serif, three lines centered. Small mark: a single pasta pot silhouette used on the kitchen door and the dinner card.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and the dinner rota
typography.rationale: A warm display serif plus a clean grotesk — the editorial common-kitchen register.
